status: Construction audit CONFIRMED a mathematically-necessary confound (true_position is a deterministic function of symbol_counts, so input-level editing cannot isolate one from the other) -- resolved via probe-direction SUBSPACE patching (projecting onto each cell's persisted true_position probe direction, raw-activation-space-corrected for the StandardScaler), leaving the orthogonal complement (symbol_counts-relevant information) at the corrupt run's own value. Validated against P=identity (exact match to full-state patch) and P=zero (exact no-op) for all 3 harness types before use. PRIMARY metric is |delta_logit| from the subspace patch (restored_fraction is degenerate here since position_pairs' own behavioral gap is near-zero by design).
description: Tests whether the residual true_position probe signal (Phase 2: 0.037-0.072 selectivity for rnn/lstm/transformer, MLP-confirmed genuine; near-zero for mamba) causally drives accept/reject, or is a decodable-but-not-causally-used byproduct. Predicted: near-zero |delta_logit| relative to condition 1's grammar_pairs reference scale, for all 4 architectures, both seeds.

position_pairs_audit.symbol_counts_also_necessarily_differ: TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION: true_position = f(counts), so any move-token flip that changes true_position also changes symbol_counts (e.g. '>'.'<' flip changes both counts by 1 each). This pair type cannot isolate a 'true_position changed, symbol_counts unchanged' case via input-level editing alone -- see the subspace-patching protocol spec, which addresses this by patching along the probe-derived DIRECTION relevant to each quantity rather than relying on the counterfactual construction alone to separate them.

construction_confound_note: position_pairs (single late-move-flip) necessarily changes symbol_counts whenever it changes true_position -- this is a mathematical property of the task (true_position = net displacement mod 5, a deterministic function of move counts), NOT a fixable construction bug. Confirmed via audit_cyclenav_pairs' symbol_counts_also_necessarily_differ field. Resolved via probe-direction subspace patching rather than further input-level editing attempts.

DIRECT_ACCURACY_INVESTIGATION.interpretation: mamba seed7 correctly REJECTS 84% of single-late-move-flip hard negatives (vs 0% for seed0 and ~0.9% for the Phase 1 population aggregate) -- a decisive, non-subtle behavioral difference, not sampling noise (verified directly, not just via the aggregate logit-gap statistic). Its long-sequence accuracy (0.8284) is BELOW both the 0.95 threshold used to select seed0 as the architecture's representative "solving" seed AND the 0.9231 bagcount-ffn shortcut ceiling every other cell (all 4 architectures, both seeds each) hits exactly or matches closely. This is consistent with seed7 having learned a QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT solution: partial genuine position-tracking (imprecise enough to cost ~9 points of raw long-sequence accuracy relative to the clean shortcut, but precise enough to catch single-move adversarial edits the pure-shortcut seed misses entirely) -- rather than "a shortcut model that also happens to leak a small amount of decodable-but-unused true_position information," which was the null-test-violation scenario this condition was designed to detect. The subspace-patch causal effect (0.106, statistically real) is likely a genuine reflection of this different underlying mechanism, not an artifact.
DIRECT_ACCURACY_INVESTIGATION.selection_caveat: mamba seed7 was included in the P2/P3 two-seeds-per-architecture scheme (phase2_p1_verify.py's p2_p3_seed_pairs) WITHOUT independently re-verifying it meets the 0.95 solving-seed threshold used for the architecture's PRIMARY representative seed (seed0). It does not meet that threshold. This means seed7's inclusion in "uniform shortcut-only" claims (Phase 2's P2/P4 cross-cell comparisons) may not be an apples-to-apples comparison with the other 7 cells, all of which DO closely match the 0.9231 shortcut ceiling. This is a genuine methodological finding for the paper, not just a curiosity: cycle-navigation's "uniform shortcut across all architectures/seeds" claim (previously believed the clean, exception-free counterpart to marked-reversal's architecture hierarchy) has its own seed-level exception, mirroring marked-reversal's seed-dependent-mechanism story in a task previously thought to be exception-free.

overall_finding_note: 7 of 8 cells confirm the null prediction cleanly (subspace-patch |delta_logit| ratio to condition 1 reference scale: 0.0000-0.0006, i.e. true_position is decodable but not causally used at readout for those cells). mamba seed7 is the exception, but investigation (see its DIRECT_ACCURACY_INVESTIGATION field) shows this is NOT the "decodable-not-causally-used" pattern the condition was designed to detect -- it is direct behavioral+causal evidence that mamba seed7 is a qualitatively different, partially-genuine-position-tracking model that does not meet the architecture's own solving-seed threshold (0.95) used elsewhere in this pilot. This is an important, genuine finding about seed selection and cycle-navigation's previously-assumed-uniform shortcut story, not a null-test violation to explain away.
